topic: Succubus: Cross-Agent Coordination Daemon for AI Coding Agents

key_points: Go-based daemon with embedded SQLite database for shared state across AI coding agents
Supports Claude Code, Factory Droid, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Copilot CLI, Aider
MCP server + lifecycle hooks for agent integration — hooks are mandatory, MCP is opt-in
File claims with conditional UPSERT and TTL-based leases (15 min default)
Agent identity pool (ORION, VESPER, KESTREL, etc.) with session-key idempotency for resume
Kanban-style task board with dependency tracking and cycle detection
Agent room for inter-agent Q&A with @mentions and resolution tracking
Three enforcement tiers: off, nag (default), block
Dashboard embedded in binary (React 19 + Vite, no Tailwind, lucide-react icons)
Single binary, no runtime deps, MIT license, 13 stars on GitHub (as of July 2026)

stats.fact: Succubus has 13 GitHub stars and 2 forks as of July 2026
Created July 28, 2026 — less than 1 week old at time of research
Written in Go 1.26 with exactly one non-stdlib dependency (modernc.org/sqlite)
Supports 8 different AI coding tools: Claude Code, Factory Droid, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Copilot CLI, Aider
32 curated agent names in the identity pool
Default file lease TTL is 900 seconds (15 minutes)
Heartbeat thresholds: 30s interval, 90s to idle, 300s to dead
Dashboard built with React 19 + Vite, no component library, no Tailwind
File claims use conditional UPSERT with 4 release conditions (freed, expired, renewal, dead holder)
Agent identity cached at .succubus/agent-<session>.json to survive context compaction
Project identity resolved from git remote URL (normalized) → sha256[:12]

angles: Succubus solves the 'blind multi-agent' problem — multiple AI coding agents editing the same repo without knowing about each other
Hook-based registration is the key design insight: agents cannot opt out of coordination
File claim system with conditional UPSERT elegantly handles edge cases (crashed agents, expired leases, dead holders)
The 'agent room' enables inter-agent communication without human-in-the-loop
Degrade-to-nothing philosophy: if daemon is down, hooks exit silently, never blocking the agent
One daemon serves all projects on a machine via project_id partitioning
Dashboard provides real-time visibility into who is doing what — essential for human oversight
Three enforcement tiers let teams choose their comfort level with automated coordination
